questions: Should whitespace characters (spaces, tabs, newlines) be preserved exactly as they appear in the input, or should multiple consecutive spaces be collapsed into a single space?
If a punctuation character appears inside a word (e.g., 'hyphen-ated' or 'apostrophe's'), should it be removed, potentially merging words or breaking word structure?
Should the function handle Unicode whitespace or control characters (e.g., zero-width spaces) in any special way?
If the input strings contain backslashes used as escape characters in regex, should they be treated literally or as escapes?
Should the function preserve the case of the original strings, or normalize to lower/upper case?
What should happen if the input is not a string (e.g., integer, None)? Should it raise an error or attempt conversion?
Should the removal be applied only to the exact characters in string.punctuation, or also to their Unicode full-width equivalents (e.g., '！' vs '!')?
If a punctuation character is part of a larger multi-character sequence (e.g., '...' or '--'), should each individual character be removed, potentially leaving spaces?
